preDonation.title: Before Donation
section1Points: Get enough sleep (at least 6-8 hours) the night before donating.
Eat a light, non-fatty meal before donating.
Drink plenty of water (about 500ml) before donating to make the blood collection process easier.
Avoid using alcohol, beer, and stimulants within 24 hours prior to donating.
section2Points: Bring your Identity Card (CCCD/ID Card or Passport).
Ensure you feel completely healthy, without cold or cough.
If taking medication, inform the screening doctor immediately.

postDonation.title: Post-Donation Care
section1Points: Rest on-site for at least 15 minutes, drink plenty of water and have light snacks provided by the organizers.
Only stand up when you feel truly comfortable. If you feel dizzy, immediately notify the medical staff.
Keep the bandage on the venipuncture site for at least 4-6 hours to prevent infection.
section2Points: Drink more water than usual (about 2-3 liters/day) to replenish lost fluids.
Supplement Iron-rich foods: beef, liver, beans, spinach, wood ear mushrooms.
Increase Vitamin C (oranges, lemons, guavas) to help the body absorb Iron better.
Do not do strenuous exercise or carry heavy objects with the donated arm for the first 24 hours.

benefits.title: Amazing Benefits of Blood Donation
section1Points: Stimulates bone marrow to produce new red blood cells, improving blood circulation.
Reduces the risk of iron overload in the body, helping to protect the cardiovascular system and liver.
Opportunity for a free health check: blood pressure, heart rate measurement, and screening for blood-borne diseases.
Burns a certain amount of calories, supporting metabolism.
section2Points: Each of your blood donations can save up to 3 patients.
Contributes to replenishing the national reserve blood supply for emergency and treatment.
Receive a Volunteer Blood Donation Certificate (valid for free blood reimbursement at public health facilities when needed).
